patterns.note: A two-column grid layout is used consistently, with a narrower left column for text-based content (project titles, descriptions) and a wider, full-bleed right column dedicated to large imagery.

The typography is minimalist, using a single sans-serif font family across the entire site. Text sizes are generally small, with subtle variations to denote hierarchy rather than dramatic scale changes.

The site employs a stark monochromatic base of white backgrounds and black text, with a subtle light grey for secondary information. All vibrant color is introduced solely through the full-bleed artwork images.

As the user scrolls down the page, the main header remains sticky at the top. The content on the left (project titles) scrolls, and in sync with this, the large images on the right column are revealed or swapped to correspond with the currently highlighted text entry.

Each project is presented as a distinct section, defined by its title and metadata in the left column, and its corresponding large-scale artwork image in the right column, creating a gallery-like browsing experience.

technique_notes: The site uses a sticky header that remains fixed at the top of the viewport during scroll. The main content area is structured as a two-column layout where the left column contains a scrolling list of text entries. The right column displays large, full-bleed images that are dynamically revealed or swapped to align with the text entry currently in focus within the left column's scroll area, creating a synchronized visual experience.

design_tokens.type_scale: minimalist, flat scale with small sans-serif text for all elements; headings are only slightly larger than body text, creating a subtle hierarchy.
design_tokens.spacing: airy, with generous vertical spacing between project entries and full-bleed imagery that fills the right column.

standout: The site's standout feature is its highly synchronized two-column scroll, where a minimalist text list on the left drives the reveal of large, full-bleed artwork on the right. This creates an immersive, gallery-like browsing experience that prioritizes the visual impact of the art while maintaining a clean, editorial feel.
